title: The Milky Way above La Silla
caption: The Milky Way above the ESO 1-meter Schmidt telescope, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The Milky Way arches across the sky above ESO's La Silla Observatory. The instrument beneath it is the ESO 1-meter Schmidt telescope, one of the facilities at this site in northern Chile.

The arch is our own galaxy seen from the inside. We live within a flattened disc of stars, gas and dust, so when we look along that disc, the light of countless distant stars merges into a pale band that wraps around the sky.

La Silla sits 2400 meters up, on the fringe of the Atacama Desert, some 600 km from Santiago de Chile to the south. Being so far from city lights gives the observatory one of the darkest night skies on the planet, which helps a band as faint as this stand out above the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla Observatory. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way appears brighter and more detailed here than it would to an observer standing beside the telescope.

explore: A Schmidt telescope is a design that trades fine detail on a single object for a wide field of view, which makes it well suited to surveying large patches of sky.
alt: The Milky Way arching across a dark sky above the ESO 1-meter Schmidt telescope at La Silla Observatory.
